facts.source: Ala. Code 34-8-1 (as amended by Act 2024-277); Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors
facts.fact: Commercial general contractors in Alabama are licensed by the Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors. Since October 1, 2024 (Act 2024-277), a license is required when the cost of the undertaking, including labor and materials, is $100,000 or more; the old threshold was $50,000. Subcontractors performing contracts of $100,000 or more must also be licensed.
facts.note: Confirmed on the board's law page and its Act 2024-277 notice: https://genconbd.alabama.gov/law/ and https://genconbd.alabama.gov/14104/changes-to-the-alabama-licensing-board-for-general-contractors-section-of-the-code-of-alabama/ ; statute text at https://law.justia.com/codes/alabama/title-34/chapter-8/section-34-8-1/

facts.source: Ala. Code 34-8-1(b); Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors
facts.fact: In Alabama, anyone who builds, supervises, repairs or renovates a swimming pool for compensation must hold a general contractor license from the Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors when the work is over $5,000, a much lower threshold than the $100,000 rule for other commercial work.
facts.note: Statute: https://law.justia.com/codes/alabama/title-34/chapter-8/section-34-8-1/ (2025 code says 'exceeding $5,000'); board law page phrases it as '$5,000 or more': https://genconbd.alabama.gov/law/

facts.source: Ala. Code 34-14A-2; Alabama Home Builders Licensure Board
facts.fact: Residential construction in Alabama is licensed separately by the Home Builders Licensure Board. A residential home builder license is required when the cost of the undertaking exceeds $10,000, and residential roofers must be licensed when the roofing job exceeds $2,500.

facts.source: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors, Testing page; PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Alabama General Contractors (updated 1/23/26)
facts.fact: Alabama general contractor exams are given by PSI. Applicants (since January 22, 2008) must pass a trade exam for their classification plus the Business and Law exam. The Business and Law exam is 50 questions, 120 minutes, open book, and needs 70% to pass; the one reference is the NASCLA Contractor's Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, Alabama General, 3rd edition.
facts.note: https://genconbd.alabama.gov/licensees/testing/ and PSI bulletin https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/76 . References may be highlighted/tabbed with permanent tabs only; no loose papers.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Alabama General Contractors (updated 1/23/26)
facts.fact: Alabama offers the NASCLA-accredited Commercial General Building Contractor exam (115 questions, 330 minutes, 81 correct to pass) as a trade exam option. The Building Contractor Under Four Stories exam is 90 questions in 230 minutes with 70% (63 correct) needed to pass.

facts.source: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors, Reciprocity and How to Apply pages
facts.fact: Alabama's general contractor board has reciprocity with Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina and Tennessee. A licensee in good standing in a comparable classification (licensed 1 year) may have the trade exam waived, but the Business and Law exam is never waived, and the application must be on file 30 days before a reciprocal license issues.
facts.note: https://genconbd.alabama.gov/licensees/reciprocity/ and https://genconbd.alabama.gov/licensees/apply/ . Board page does not mention NASCLA reciprocity beyond offering the NASCLA exam.

facts.source: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors, How to Apply page
facts.fact: Prime contractor applications to the Alabama general contractor board must be on file 30 days before a quarterly board meeting. Subcontractor applicants must submit three references from general contractors, architects, engineers or awarding authorities, and a subcontractor may bid to a general contractor but cannot start work until licensed.
facts.note: https://genconbd.alabama.gov/licensees/apply/ . Financial statement and bid-limit rules are in Ala. Admin. Code 230-X-1-.02 and -.19 but were not readable in this session.

facts.source: Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors, Renewal Information page
facts.fact: Alabama general contractor license renewals are staggered by month according to the first letter of the company name and are filed online. If a license is not renewed within one year after expiration, the contractor must reapply and retake the trade and Business and Law exams.
facts.note: https://genconbd.alabama.gov/licensees/renewal-information/ . The page does not mention continuing education for general contractors.

facts.source: Alabama Electrical Contractors Board
facts.fact: Electrical work in Alabama is licensed statewide by the Alabama Electrical Contractors Board, which issues electrical contractor licenses and journeyman electrician licenses. Electrical contractors must complete 14 hours of continuing education for renewal (per the board's 2027 renewal notice).
facts.note: https://aecb.alabama.gov/ (home page notice). Journeyman CE hours were not stated on the page.

facts.source: Ala. Code 34-37-1; Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board
facts.fact: The Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board certifies master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, master gas fitters, journeyman gas fitters and registered apprentices, all on annual certificates. A plumbing or gas business must register a certified master as its principal, and medical gas piping work needs an added medical gas certificate.
facts.note: Statute: https://law.justia.com/codes/alabama/title-34/chapter-37/section-34-37-1/ . Board site https://pgfb.alabama.gov/ says CE for 2027 renewals must be done before November 1, 2026 (renewal window Oct 1 to Dec 31).

facts.source: Ala. Code 34-31-18 et seq.; Alabama Board of Heating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors
facts.fact: HVAC and refrigeration contractors in Alabama are certified by testing through the State Board of Heating, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors.
facts.note: Board name confirmed in Ala. Code 34-31-18 (https://law.justia.com/codes/alabama/title-34/chapter-31/section-34-31-18/), but the board website blocked fetching, so certification classes, exam provider and CE were not confirmed.

facts.source: Ala. Code 35-11-210
facts.fact: In Alabama, a supplier or subcontractor without a direct contract with the owner gets a lien for the full price only if it notifies the owner in writing before furnishing the material (and the owner does not object in writing before it is used). Without that notice, the lien is limited to the unpaid balance the owner still owes the contractor.

facts.source: Ala. Code 35-11-215; Ala. Code 35-11-221
facts.fact: Alabama lien statements must be filed with the probate judge within 6 months after the last work or materials for an original contractor, within 30 days for journeymen and day laborers, and within 4 months for everyone else (subs and suppliers). A suit to enforce the lien must be filed within 6 months after the entire debt matures.

facts.source: A.R.S. 32-1121(A)(14); Arizona Registrar of Contractors
facts.fact: Arizona contractors (general and trade) are licensed by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC). The 'handyman' exemption covers only jobs with a total price, including labor and materials, under $1,000 that do not need a building permit, and the person may not advertise without stating 'not a licensed contractor'.

facts.source: Arizona Registrar of Contractors, Applying for a License
facts.fact: An Arizona ROC license needs a qualifying party who is regularly employed by the business, at least 18, and meets the classification's minimum years of experience. Applicants and qualifying parties must submit a background check (valid 90 days) and proof of a license bond.
facts.note: https://azroc.gov/applying-for-a-license . Experience years per classification are in the ROC License Classification Requirements form (not read in this session).

facts.source: Arizona Registrar of Contractors, Applying for a License; PSI AZ ROC Candidate Information Bulletin (2/18/2026)
facts.fact: Arizona applicants take the Statutes and Rules Exam (SRE), an online ROC course plus test delivered through Gmetrix that cannot be waived, and a trade exam through PSI that requires 70% to pass. The SRE is required for applicants not listed as a qualifying party on an Arizona license within the last five years.
facts.note: https://azroc.gov/applying-for-a-license and PSI bulletin https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/5617 . Question counts/time are in each trade's content outline, not the main bulletin.

facts.source: Arizona Registrar of Contractors, Applying for a License; Ariz. Admin. Code R4-9-106(E)
facts.fact: Arizona B-1 and B-2 general commercial applicants may take the NASCLA Commercial General Building exam in place of the ROC trade exam, and CR-11, C-11 and R-11 electrical applicants may take the NASCLA electrical exam. The trade exam (not the SRE) can be waived if the qualifying party qualified a license in good standing in the same or comparable classification within the past five years.

Arizona license bonds depend on license type and estimated annual volume. Under A.R.S. 32-1152 the range is $5,000 to $15,000 for a residential general (B) license and $1,000 to $7,500 for residential specialty; commercial general bonds run from $5,000 (under $150,000 volume) up to $50,000 to $100,000 ($10 million or more). Residential contractors must also join the Residential Contractors' Recovery Fund or post an extra $200,000 bond.
facts.note: Statute: https://www.azleg.gov/ars/32/01152.htm . Exact amounts within each range are set by ROC rule.

facts.fact: In Arizona, a contractor cannot sue to collect payment for work that requires a license unless it alleges and proves it was properly licensed both when the contract was made and when the claim arose.

facts.source: Arizona Registrar of Contractors license classifications
facts.fact: Arizona licenses electrical (e.g., R-11, C-11, CR-11), plumbing (R-37, C-37, CR-37) and HVAC (R-39, C-39, CR-39) work as ROC contractor classifications with residential (R), commercial (C) and dual (CR) versions. Arizona does not issue a statewide journeyman or master electrician or plumber license; individual worker certification, if any, is local.
facts.note: Classification codes R-11/C-11/CR-11 are confirmed on https://azroc.gov/applying-for-a-license; the plumbing/HVAC codes and the absence of state journeyman licensing come from general knowledge and were not confirmed on an official page this session.

facts.fact: Arizona requires a preliminary twenty-day notice as a condition of any lien: it must be served on the owner, original contractor, construction lender and the party the claimant contracted with no later than 20 days after the claimant first furnishes labor or materials. A late notice covers only work furnished within 20 days before it was served and afterward; wage laborers are exempt.

An Arizona notice and claim of lien must be recorded within 120 days after completion of the improvement, or within 60 days after a notice of completion is recorded. The lien lapses 6 months after recording unless a foreclosure suit is filed and a notice of pendency of action is recorded within that time.
In Arizona, a person who is required to be licensed as a contractor but does not hold a valid license has no mechanics' lien rights.

An Arizona contractor license is suspended by law the business day after its renewal date unless a renewal with a valid bond and fee was received or mailed by that date. A suspended license may be renewed within one year (with an added fee); after one year a new application is required. Arizona ROC licenses renew every two years and there is no continuing education requirement.
facts.note: Suspension and one-year reactivation rules confirmed at https://www.azleg.gov/ars/32/01125.htm ; the two-year renewal cycle and no-CE statement were not confirmed on an official page this session.

facts.source: Ark. Code 17-25-101; Arkansas Contractors Licensing Board (Dept. of Labor and Licensing)
facts.fact: The Arkansas Contractors Licensing Board requires a commercial contractor license when the cost of work, including labor and materials, is $50,000 or more. Any project that is not a single-family residence counts as commercial, and a business and law exam is required.

facts.source: Arkansas Contractors Licensing Board, Apply for License page
facts.fact: In Arkansas, a subcontractor working under a properly licensed prime contractor on a commercial job can use a subcontractor registration certificate instead of a full license. If the prime contractor lacks the proper commercial license, the subcontractor needs a commercial license, and a contract directly with the owner is prime contracting.

facts.source: Ark. Code 17-25-502, -513; Residential Building Contractors Committee law (rev. July 2025)
facts.fact: Residential work in Arkansas (single-family = 1 to 4 units) is licensed by the Residential Building Contractors Committee of the Contractors Licensing Board, which issues residential builder, remodeler and specialty (home improvement) licenses. Projects of $2,000 or less are exempt, but splitting a job into contracts under $2,000 does not qualify.
facts.note: https://labor.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/Residential-Law-revised-July-2025.pdf ; the board page says the home improvement license applies to specialty work over $2,000 on a single-family residence.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Arkansas Contractors Licensing Board (updated 6/3/2022)
facts.fact: Every Arkansas contractor classification must pass the Arkansas Contractor Business and Law exam plus any trade exam. The Business and Law exam is 50 questions, 120 minutes, open book, and needs 35 correct (70%); the only allowed reference is the NASCLA Contractor's Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, Arkansas edition (8th edition in the 2022 bulletin).
facts.note: PSI bulletin: https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/6936 . Bulletin is dated 2022; confirm the current required edition before testing. An older Prometric bulletin (2019) used the 6th edition.

facts.source: Ark. Code 17-25-304; ACLB Bond in Lieu of Financial Statement form
facts.fact: Arkansas commercial applicants must submit a financial statement reviewed by a CPA or licensed public accountant (a compiled statement is allowed for a single project under $1,500,000). Instead, they may post a surety bond of 10 times the required net worth for the classification, e.g., $500,000 for Building or Heavy, $200,000 for Light Building, Mechanical or Electrical, and $50,000 for Specialty.

Arkansas residential builders and unlimited remodelers/specialty contractors must file a sworn compiled financial statement showing positive net worth for work of $50,000 or more, and must show workers' compensation coverage before a license is issued or renewed. A lapse in workers' comp coverage requires the committee to revoke the license.

facts.source: Ark. Code 17-25-515
facts.fact: An Arkansas residential contractor who works without the required license cannot sue to enforce the contract or recover under quantum meruit.

facts.source: Arkansas Dept. of Labor and Licensing, Electrical Inspection and Licensing
facts.fact: The Arkansas Board of Electrical Examiners (Dept. of Labor and Licensing) licenses master, journeyman, residential master and residential journeyman electricians, plus air conditioning and industrial maintenance electricians, and registers apprentices.

facts.source: Arkansas Dept. of Labor and Licensing, HVAC/R
facts.fact: Arkansas HVAC/R licenses (Classes A, B, D and E among others) are issued through the Department of Labor and Licensing and the State HVAC/R Board; applicants must be pre-approved by the board to sit for the exam. The HVAC/R board has no reciprocal licensing agreements with other states.
facts.note: https://labor.arkansas.gov/labor/code-enforcement/hvac-r/ . The page did not describe the scope of each class.

facts.source: Arkansas Department of Health, Plumbing and Natural Gas Section
facts.fact: Plumbers in Arkansas are licensed by the Arkansas Department of Health (Plumbing and Natural Gas Section), not the Contractors Licensing Board, with master and journeyman plumber licenses.
facts.note: The Department of Health page could not be fetched this session; based on general knowledge and secondary sites.

facts.source: Ark. Code 18-44-115
facts.fact: On Arkansas residential jobs (4 or fewer units), the contractor must give the owner the statutory lien notice before work begins, or neither the contractor nor anyone else can claim a lien (unless a payment and performance bond is provided). On commercial jobs, subs, suppliers and laborers must send the owner and contractor a notice of nonpayment within 75 days after furnishing labor or materials to keep lien rights.

An Arkansas lien claimant must give the owner 10 days' notice before filing, then file the lien with the circuit clerk within 120 days after the last materials or labor were furnished. A suit to enforce the lien must be commenced within 15 months after filing.

Arkansas residential licenses expire one year after issuance unless the committee offers a two- or three-year renewal. A license may be renewed up to two years after expiration (with a late fee within 30 days); after that a new application is needed.

facts.source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7048 (as amended by AB 1170, eff. Jan. 1, 2026); Contractors State License Board
facts.fact: California contractors are licensed by the Contractors State License Board (CSLB). The minor work exemption covers only small, non-substantial jobs with a total price (labor, materials and everything else) under $1,000 that need no building permit; it does not apply if the work is part of a larger job, is split up to evade the law, or the person advertises as a contractor or hires others to help.
facts.note: Statute text (2025 code reflecting AB 1170, effective 1/1/2026): https://law.justia.com/codes/california/code-bpc/division-3/chapter-9/article-3/section-7048/ . The limit was $500 for many years; older study materials still say $500.

facts.source: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16, 825
facts.fact: A California license applicant (or qualifier) needs at least 4 years of experience at the journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor level in the classification, gained within the 10 years before applying. Accredited schooling or an approved apprenticeship can count for up to 3 of the 4 years.

facts.source: CSLB Apply for a License and Contractor License pages; Bus. & Prof. Code 7065
facts.fact: California applicants must pass two CSLB exams, Law and Business and a trade exam (no trade exam for the C-61 Limited Specialty class), and then complete the Asbestos Open Book Exam. No exam is needed if the person served as a qualifier in good standing for the same classification, or passed both exams, within the past five years.
facts.note: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Applicants and https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Applicants/Contractors_License/ . Question counts and time limits were not stated on the pages fetched.

facts.source: CSLB Bond Requirements page; Bus. & Prof. Code 7071.6
facts.fact: Since January 1, 2023, every active California contractor license must carry a $25,000 contractor's bond, and a responsible managing employee qualifier must post a separate $25,000 Bond of Qualifying Individual. A disciplinary bond, when ordered, is at least $25,000 and up to 10 times the contractor's bond.

facts.source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7031
facts.fact: A California contractor who needed a license cannot sue to collect payment unless it was duly licensed at all times during the work, and an owner who hired an unlicensed contractor can sue to recover all compensation already paid (disgorgement).

facts.source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7159
facts.fact: California home improvement contracts over $500 must follow B&P 7159: the down payment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less, and the buyer may cancel within 3 business days after receiving the signed contract (5 days for senior citizen buyers).

facts.source: CSLB license classifications; Cal. Labor Code 3099-3099.4 (DIR electrician certification)
facts.fact: California licenses electrical, plumbing and HVAC businesses as CSLB specialty contractors (C-10 Electrical, C-36 Plumbing, C-20 Warm-Air HVAC). Workers doing electrical work for a C-10 contractor must also hold a state electrician certification from the Department of Industrial Relations (e.g., General Electrician), or be registered apprentices. There is no statewide journeyman plumber or HVAC license.
facts.note: Classification codes and the DIR certification rule are from general knowledge; the CSLB classification page and DIR pages failed to load this session, so details (and hour requirements) were not confirmed.

facts.source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7140; CSLB Reciprocity page
facts.fact: California contractor licenses run for two years from the last day of the month issued, and a timely renewal continues the license another two years. CSLB has reciprocity programs with Arizona, Louisiana and Nevada.
facts.note: https://codes.findlaw.com/ca/business-and-professions-code/bpc-sect-7140/ and https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Applicants/Reciprocity/ . The reciprocity page did not state which exam is waived (commonly the trade exam, with Law and Business still required).

facts.source: Cal. Civil Code 8204
facts.fact: In California, a preliminary notice must be given no later than 20 days after the claimant first furnishes work. A late notice still works, but lien, stop payment notice and payment bond rights then cover only work performed within 20 days before the notice was served and after.

facts.source: Cal. Civil Code 8412, 8414, 8460
facts.fact: A California direct contractor must record its lien after finishing its contract and before the earlier of 90 days after completion of the project or 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. Other claimants (subs, suppliers) have the earlier of 90 days after completion or 30 days after a notice of completion or cessation. A suit to enforce the lien must be filed within 90 days after recording.

facts.source: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations (DORA); local building departments
facts.fact: Colorado has no statewide general contractor license. General, building and specialty contractors are licensed or registered by cities and counties (for example Denver, Colorado Springs/Pikes Peak Regional Building Department), often with ICC exams, while the state (DORA) licenses only electricians and plumbers among the construction trades.
facts.note: Consistent across many secondary sources and with DORA's program list, but no official state page saying 'no state GC license' was confirmed this session.

facts.source: C.R.S. 12-115-110; Colorado State Electrical Board (DORA)
facts.fact: The Colorado State Electrical Board licenses Master Electricians, Journeyman Electricians and Residential Wiremen. A journeyman needs at least 4 years of apprenticeship or practical experience (at least 2 years commercial/industrial) plus 288 hours of training in safety and the NEC; a residential wireman needs 2 years of training or experience in 1- to 4-family dwellings.
facts.note: Board page https://dpo.colorado.gov/Electrical ; statute text via FindLaw https://codes.findlaw.com/co/title-12-professions-and-occupations/co-rev-st-sect-12-115-110/

facts.fact: A Colorado Master Electrician applicant generally needs at least one year of experience planning, laying out and supervising electrical work beyond the journeyman requirements (other routes: an engineering graduate with one year of practical construction experience, or a trade school graduate with four years of practical experience). The board or its designee conducts the exam.

facts.source: Colorado State Electrical Board (DORA) homepage
facts.fact: Colorado Residential Wiremen, Journeyman and Master Electricians must complete 24 hours of continuing education during each 3-year license period, from board-attested providers. The current licenses expire September 30, 2026, with renewal allowed through November 30, 2026.
facts.note: https://dpo.colorado.gov/Electrical . Those first licensed by exam in the current period need no CE until after their first renewal.

facts.source: C.R.S. 12-155-110; Colorado State Plumbing Board (DORA)
facts.fact: The Colorado State Plumbing Board licenses Residential Plumbers, Journeyworker Plumbers ('journeyman' renamed effective July 1, 2025) and Master Plumbers. By statute the board may require up to 3,400 hours of practical experience for residential, 6,800 hours for journeyworker and 8,500 hours for master; a board-approved plumbing program counts as one year of experience.
facts.note: https://dpo.colorado.gov/Plumbing ; statute via FindLaw https://codes.findlaw.com/co/title-12-professions-and-occupations/co-rev-st-sect-12-155-110/ (statute gives maximums; the board rule sets the actual minimums).

facts.source: Colorado State Plumbing Board (DORA) homepage
facts.fact: Colorado plumbing licenses run for a two-year period. Active Residential, Journeyworker and Master Plumbers must complete at least 8 hours of continuing education each licensure year (March 1 through February 28) from board-attested providers.

facts.source: Local building departments
facts.fact: Colorado does not issue a state HVAC or mechanical license; mechanical contractors are licensed by local jurisdictions where required.
facts.note: Based on DORA's program list (only electrical and plumbing boards) and secondary sources; not confirmed on an official page this session.

facts.fact: In Colorado, a lien claimant must serve a notice of intent on the owner and prime contractor at least 10 days before filing the lien statement. Most claimants must file within 4 months after their last labor or materials; day or piece laborers who furnish no materials must file within 2 months after the structure is completed. Abandoning work for 3 months counts as completion.

A Colorado mechanics' lien expires unless an action to enforce it is started, and a notice of the action (lis pendens) recorded, within 6 months after the last work or materials or completion of the improvement.

facts.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 20-341gg et seq., 29-276b; CT Department of Consumer Protection (Major Contractor)
facts.fact: Connecticut has no general 'GC license' by dollar amount; instead the Department of Consumer Protection registers Major Contractors, who build, structurally alter or demolish structures that exceed the threshold in C.G.S. 29-276b (4 stories, 60 feet tall, 150,000 sq ft of gross floor area, or occupancy of 1,000 persons), and subs doing structural work for them. Major Contractor registrations expire annually on June 30.

facts.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 20-419, 20-420, 20-427 (Home Improvement Act)
facts.fact: Connecticut home improvement contractors and salespersons must register with the Department of Consumer Protection. Jobs of $200 or less are not 'home improvement', and a person whose home improvement contracts total $1,000 or less in any 12 months is not a 'contractor'. Registrations expire annually on March 31.
facts.note: Statute text: https://www.cga.ct.gov/current/pub/chap_400.htm (check the date; older materials say Nov. 30 expiration).

facts.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 20-429, 20-432
facts.fact: A Connecticut home improvement contract is not valid or enforceable against the owner unless it is in writing, signed by both parties, and includes the contractor's registration number, start and completion dates, and notice of the owner's cancellation rights. Homeowners harmed by a registered contractor can collect up to $25,000 per claim from the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund after a judgment or arbitration award.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, CT DCP Electrical Trades (updated 2/4/2026)
facts.fact: Connecticut electricians are licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection with contractor and journeyperson tiers, e.g., E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor (100 questions, 4 hours) and E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson (80 questions, 3.5 hours). PSI gives the exams, which are open book (NEC 2020 or 2023) and need 70% to pass.
facts.note: https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/49 . Limited licenses include C-5/C-6, L-1/L-2, PV-1/PV-2, T-1/T-2.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, CT DCP Heating, Piping and Cooling Trades (updated 2/4/2026)
facts.fact: Connecticut heating, piping and cooling licenses come in contractor/journeyperson pairs, such as S-1 Unlimited Heating, Piping and Cooling Contractor (80 questions, 3 hours) and S-2 Journeyperson (70 questions, 3 hours), and D-1/D-2 Limited Warm Air, AC and Refrigeration. All PSI exams are open book with a 70% passing score.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletins, CT DCP Occupational Licensing (updated 2/4/2026)
facts.fact: In Connecticut's trade licensing, journeypersons take only the trade exam, while contractors also take the Business and Law exam: 50 questions, 2 hours, 70% (35 correct), open book with the NASCLA Contractor's Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, Connecticut 6th edition. Passed portion scores are valid for 2 years.

facts.source: CT Department of Consumer Protection, Plumbing and Piping Work Examining Board
facts.fact: Connecticut plumbers are licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection (Plumbing and Piping Work Examining Board) as P-1 Unlimited Plumbing and Piping Contractor or P-2 Unlimited Journeyperson, with limited categories as well; exams are given by PSI.
facts.note: Board name and the P-1/P-2 codes are from general knowledge and secondary sites; the PSI plumbing bulletin was not located this session.

facts.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 49-34; 49-35
facts.fact: A Connecticut mechanic's lien certificate must be lodged with the town clerk within 90 days after the claimant stops work, and a copy served on the owner within 30 days after lodging. Subcontractors and suppliers without a direct contract must also give the owner and original contractor written notice of intent to claim a lien no later than 90 days after ceasing work.

facts.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. 49-39
facts.fact: A Connecticut mechanic's lien expires unless the claimant starts a foreclosure action and records a lis pendens within one year from the date the lien was recorded.

facts.source: 30 Del. C. 2502; Delaware Division of Revenue
facts.fact: Delaware has no competency-based statewide general contractor license or exam. Instead, anyone doing business as a contractor must get a contractor business license from the Division of Revenue before signing a contract (for competitively bid contracts over $50,000, the application must be started with the bid), and must show workers' compensation coverage. The license runs to January 1 and renews yearly.
facts.note: Statute text: https://delcode.delaware.gov/title30/c025/index.html . Contractors also pay a gross receipts license fee under 2502(c).

facts.fact: In Delaware, architects, engineers, contractors and construction managers must report to the Department of Finance within 10 days after entering any contract with a nonresident contractor or subcontractor, listing the contract value and the parties. Violations carry a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per occurrence.

facts.source: Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners (Division of Professional Regulation)
facts.fact: The Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners licenses Master, Master Special, Limited and Limited Special electricians, journeypersons and apprentices. A Master needs 6 years of full-time experience (or 4 years under a Master plus 2 years of technical training); a Limited needs 3 years under a Master or Limited electrician. Master and Limited licensees must carry general liability insurance of at least $300,000.

facts.source: Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners, Exam Information page
facts.fact: Delaware electrical exams are given by ProV (in person in Delaware or online through Examroom), are based on the NEC edition currently adopted in Delaware, and need a minimum score of 75% to pass. Candidates must be approved by the board, with documents submitted at least 45 days before the test date.

facts.source: Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners, Continuing Education page
facts.fact: Delaware electrical licenses renew on a two-year cycle ending June 30 of even-numbered years. Master, Master Special, Limited and Limited Special electricians need 10 CE hours per full renewal period (5 on the NEC from the second renewal), and journeypersons, residential and apprentices need 5 hours.

facts.source: Delaware Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners
facts.fact: Delaware's Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners licenses Master Plumbers, Master HVACR and Master Restricted HVACR. Applicants need 2 years under a master after earning a journeyman certificate, or 7 years under a master without one (plus an Apprenticeship By-Pass Exam), and must pass the master exam with at least 70%.
facts.note: https://dpr.delaware.gov/boards/plumbers/newlicense/ and https://dpr.delaware.gov/boards/plumbers/hvacrlicensure/ . Connecticut, Iowa and Maryland master licenses are treated as substantially similar.

facts.source: Delaware Board of Plumbing/HVACR Examiners, Continuing Education page
facts.fact: Delaware plumbing and HVACR licensees need 5 hours of continuing education for each renewal after the first (first renewal is prorated at 0, 3 or 5 hours depending on when the license was issued).
facts.note: https://dpr.delaware.gov/boards/plumbers/continuing-education-and-audit-information/ . Regulations were updated in March 2025 (24 Del. Admin. Code 1800).

facts.fact: A Delaware contractor who contracted directly with the owner must file its mechanics' lien statement of claim within 180 days after the structure is completed; subcontractors and suppliers must file within 120 days after completing their labor or last delivering materials. The claim is enforced by a writ of scire facias in Superior Court.

In Delaware, no lien can be obtained against a residence when the owner has made full and final payment to the contractor in good faith, and the contractor must give a notarized certification of full payment or a release of liens before getting final payment. A contractor or sub who fails to give the owner a requested list of suppliers and workers within 10 days loses its right to further payment and lien remedies.

facts.source: DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection (DLCP), contractor insurance page; 17 DCMR 3902
facts.fact: In the District of Columbia, general contractors and construction managers obtain a Basic Business License (General Contractor/Construction Manager category) from the Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection (DLCP). The application must include a certificate of insurance showing commercial general liability under 17 DCMR 3902 from an insurer rated B+ or better by A.M. Best, kept in force through the license period and project completion.
facts.note: https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616016 and https://dob.dc.gov/page/license-types-requiring-insurance . Coverage dollar amounts were not shown on these pages.

facts.source: DC DLCP contractor insurance page
facts.fact: DC home improvement contractors need a Home Improvement Contractor Basic Business License from DLCP and must file a certificate of insurance naming DLCP as certificate holder, issued to the registered business at its premises address (no P.O. boxes).
facts.note: https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616016 . A home improvement bond is also commonly required, but the amount was not confirmed on an official page this session.

facts.source: DC Board of Industrial Trades (DLCP)
facts.fact: The DC Board of Industrial Trades licenses electricians (apprentice, journeyman, master, contractor), plumbers/gasfitters (apprentice, journeyman, master, contractor), refrigeration and air conditioning, asbestos, elevator and steam/operating engineer trades. A Trade Contractor registration requires a designated DC-licensed master tradesperson and a bond, and exams are given by PSI.

facts.source: DC Board of Industrial Trades (DLCP)
facts.fact: DC industrial trade licenses run up to 2 years and expire on fixed dates: electrician licenses November 30 of odd years, plumber/gasfitter licenses March 31 of even years, and refrigeration and air conditioning licenses September 30 of even years.
facts.note: https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1619081 . The page did not mention CE requirements.

facts.source: DLCP Refrigeration and Air Conditioning license guide
facts.fact: DC refrigeration and air conditioning licenses come in apprentice, journeyman and master levels, each Regular or Limited (Limited = equipment at or below 25 compressor horsepower). Journeyman by exam needs 3 years of experience and master needs 5 years, plus EPA CFC Universal certification; the exam is open book (International Mechanical Code 2012 and Modern Refrigeration and Air Conditioning).

facts.source: DC Board of Industrial Trades
facts.fact: DC master electrician applicants generally need several years of experience as a licensed journeyman, and electrical exams are open book based on the NEC; electrical contractors must designate a DC-licensed master electrician.
facts.note: Master/contractor structure confirmed at https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1619081 , but the specific experience years and exam format for electricians could not be confirmed (DLCP electrical guide did not load).

facts.fact: A DC mechanic's lien claimant must record a notice of intent to hold a lien in the land records during construction or within 90 days after the earlier of completion or termination of the project; otherwise the lien is lost.
A suit to enforce a DC mechanic's lien must be filed within 180 days after the notice of intent is recorded in the land records.

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 489.105; Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
facts.fact: Florida contractors are licensed by the Construction Industry Licensing Board (CILB) under the Department of Business and Professional Regulation. A certified contractor holds a statewide certificate and may contract anywhere in Florida; a registered contractor met only a local jurisdiction's competency requirements and may contract only there. Division I covers general, building and residential contractors; Division II covers trades such as plumbing, Class A/B/C air conditioning, mechanical, roofing and pool.

Florida's minor work exemption applies only when the total contract price for labor, materials and everything else is less than $2,500, the job is not part of a larger operation or split up to evade the law, and the person does not advertise as a contractor. Owner-builders may build one- or two-family homes for their own use (and commercial buildings up to $75,000); selling or leasing within one year of completion is presumed a violation.

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 489.111
facts.fact: To sit for a Florida certified contractor exam, an applicant must be at least 18, of good moral character, and generally have 4 years of active experience in the trade, at least 1 year of it as a foreman; alternatively, up to 3 years of college credit plus at least 1 year as a foreman.

facts.source: DBPR Bureau of Education and Testing CILB FAQ (updated June 26, 2012)
facts.fact: Florida CILB exams are registered through Professional Testing, Inc. (PTI), with the Business and Finance exam given by Pearson VUE. Per the DBPR FAQ, Business and Finance has 120 questions (84 correct = 70% to pass) and candidates may bring approved reference books; scores are not rounded.
facts.note: https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/servop/testing/documents/cilb_faq.pdf is dated 2012; vendors, question counts and timing may have changed since. Confirm with the current PTI/Pearson VUE candidate bulletin.

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 489.115; Fla. Admin. Code R. 61G4-15.003
facts.fact: Florida applicants must submit a credit report and prove financial responsibility; board rules may require net worth, cash or bonding of up to $20,000 for Division I and $10,000 for Division II (half can be met with a 14-hour financial responsibility course). Minimum insurance is $300,000 public liability and $50,000 property damage for general and building contractors, and $100,000/$25,000 for residential and most Division II contractors, plus workers' compensation.
facts.note: Statute: http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0489/Sections/0489.115.html ; rule text via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/florida/Fla-Admin-Code-Ann-R-61G4-15-003

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 489.115
facts.fact: Florida contractor certificates and registrations renew every 2 years. Each renewal needs at least 14 classroom hours of continuing education, including workers' compensation, business practices and workplace safety (plus wind mitigation for applicable categories), with 1 hour on laws and rules.

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 489.511 (Part II, Electrical and Alarm System Contracting)
facts.fact: Florida electrical and alarm system contractors are licensed separately from the CILB, by the Electrical Contractors' Licensing Board. Exam eligibility options include 4 years as a supervisor or contractor in the trade within the past 8 years, 3 years of management experience within 6 years, or 6 years of combined training/education/supervisory experience within 12 years. Florida has no statewide journeyman electrician license.
facts.note: Experience options verified in statute: http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0489/Sections/0489.511.html ; the board name and 'no state journeyman license' are from general knowledge (the section does not name the board).

facts.source: Fla. Stat. 713.06
facts.fact: In Florida, lienors who are not in privity with the owner (except laborers) must serve a Notice to Owner before starting or within 45 days after first furnishing labor, services or materials, and before the owner's final payment. A contractor must give the owner a final payment affidavit at least 5 days before suing to enforce a lien.

A Florida claim of lien must be recorded within 90 days after the lienor's final furnishing and served on the owner before or within 15 days after recording. The lien expires 1 year after recording unless a suit to enforce it is filed; if the owner records a notice of contest, the lienor has only 60 days to sue.
In Florida, no construction lien exists in favor of a contractor, subcontractor or sub-subcontractor who is unlicensed under s. 489.128 or 489.532.

facts.source: HRS 444-2(4); Hawaii Contractors License Board (DCCA PVL)
facts.fact: Hawaii contractors are licensed by the Contractors License Board (DCCA Professional and Vocational Licensing), and a license is required to bid on or perform any residential, commercial or public construction. The small-project exemption in HRS 444-2 covers only jobs with a total price for labor and materials of $1,500 or less, and never applies when a building permit is required or when a project is split to evade the law.
facts.note: Official HRS text: https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/hrscurrent/Vol10_Ch0436-0474/HRS0444/HRS_0444-0002.htm . Conflict: the board's Contractor FAQ (Jan 2026, https://cca.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Contractor_FAQ-18.pdf) says '$1,000.00 or less' including taxes; reviewer should confirm.

facts.source: Hawaii Contractors License Board Contractor FAQ (Jan 2026)
facts.fact: Hawaii license categories are general engineering (A), general building (B) and specialty (C) contractors. Applicants need 4 years of verified supervisory experience in the classification applied for and proof of liability insurance and workers' compensation (if they have employees); a bond is required only if the board requires one.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Hawaii DCCA Contractor Examinations (Jan. 20, 2026)
facts.fact: Hawaii contractor exams are given by PSI (since January 2023) and must be passed within 6 months of board approval. The Business and Law exam, required for all new applicants, is 80 questions in 180 minutes, closed book, with 75% needed to pass.
facts.note: Bulletin: https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/10625 ; board exam page https://cca.hawaii.gov/pvl/boards/contractor/application-deadline-examination-dates/ . Content changes took effect March 30, 2026.

facts.source: PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, Hawaii DCCA Contractor Examinations (Jan. 20, 2026)
facts.fact: Hawaii's B General Building Contractor trade exam is 80 questions in 240 minutes, closed book, 75% to pass; the A General Engineering exam is 100 questions in 240 minutes. All Hawaii contractor trade exams use a 75% passing score.

facts.source: Hawaii Contractors License Board Contractor FAQ (Jan 2026)
facts.fact: Hawaii owner-builders may build or improve residential or farm structures for their own use without a contractor license if they register with the county building department, supervise the work, use only licensed subcontractors, do no electrical or plumbing work themselves, and do not sell or lease the structure within one year of completion.

facts.source: Hawaii Contractors License Board renewal information
facts.fact: Hawaii contractor licenses expire September 30 of every even-numbered year (current period October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2028). Unrenewed licensees are unlicensed and may not practice; a license may be restored within 60 days with a late fee, after which a new application is required. Active entities and sole proprietors must submit a tax clearance issued within 6 months.
facts.note: https://cca.hawaii.gov/pvl/boards/contractor/ ; no continuing education requirement is mentioned for contractors.

facts.source: Hawaii Board of Electricians and Plumbers (DCCA PVL)
facts.fact: Electricians and plumbers in Hawaii are licensed by the Board of Electricians and Plumbers, on 3-year renewal cycles ending June 30: electrician licenses renew in 2026, 2029 and 2032, and plumber licenses in 2027, 2030 and 2033. Electrical and plumbing contractors also need a C-13 or C-37 specialty license from the Contractors License Board.
facts.note: Renewal cycles verified at https://cca.hawaii.gov/pvl/boards/electrician/ (the page itself has an inconsistent plumber period). The C-13/C-37 contractor codes and license tiers (journeyworker, supervising electrician, master plumber) were not confirmed this session.

facts.fact: In Hawaii, a mechanic's lien starts with an application filed in circuit court and served on the owner no later than 45 days after the 'date of completion'. Completion is set when the owner or GC publishes a notice of completion twice, 7 days apart, in a local newspaper and files an affidavit of publication; if no valid notice is published, completion is treated as one year after actual completion. The court holds a probable-cause hearing 3 to 10 days after service.
facts.note: Official HRS text: https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/hrscurrent/Vol12_Ch0501-0588/HRS0507/HRS_0507-0043.htm . The enforcement-suit deadline was not found in HRS 507-47 text and is omitted.

facts.source: Idaho Code 54-5204, 54-5205; Idaho Contractors Board (DOPL)
facts.fact: Idaho has no general contractor competency license or exam; instead, contractors must register with the Idaho Contractors Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses) before doing business or advertising as a contractor. Casual, minor or inconsequential work with a total price under $2,000 is exempt, unless it is part of a larger project or split to evade the law.

An Idaho contractor may not hire another contractor who must be registered unless it gets proof of current registration. An unregistered, non-exempt contractor cannot sue to collect payment unless it proves it was registered or exempt the whole time it performed the work.

Separately, anyone acting as a public works contractor in Idaho needs a public works contractor license issued through DOPL. Exemptions include a single multi-trade project estimated under $100,000 and subcontract work under $100,000 performed under a contractor holding a Class Unlimited, AAA, AA or A public works license.

facts.source: Idaho Contractors Board (DOPL) page
facts.fact: Idaho contractor registrations have been annual, and the Contractors Board began transitioning to biennial registration in October 2025.

facts.source: Idaho Code 54-1007; Idaho Electrical Board (DOPL)
facts.fact: The Idaho Electrical Board issues apprentice, journeyman, master, contractor and limited electrical licenses. Journeyman candidates qualify through a registered apprenticeship (hours set by board rule) or 8 years / 16,000 hours of work experience; a master needs at least 4 years as a licensed journeyman, and both must pass an exam.
facts.note: https://legislature.idaho.gov/statutesrules/idstat/title54/t54ch10/sect54-1007/ and https://dopl.idaho.gov/elec/ (journeyman and master terms 3 years; contractor 1 year; transitioning to biennial licensure Oct. 30, 2026).

facts.source: Idaho State Plumbing Board (DOPL)
facts.fact: The Idaho State Plumbing Board licenses plumbing apprentices, journeymen and contractors (plus specialty categories); journeyman and contractor licenses run 3-year terms.

facts.source: Idaho HVAC Board (DOPL)
facts.fact: The Idaho HVAC Board licenses HVAC apprentices, journeymen and contractors, plus specialty and limited heating specialty categories; journeyman and contractor licenses run 3-year terms, with a move to biennial licensure starting October 30, 2026.

facts.source: Idaho Code 45-525
facts.fact: Before signing a residential contract over $2,000 with a homeowner, an Idaho general contractor must give a disclosure statement explaining the owner's rights to lien waivers, proof of liability and workers' comp insurance, extended title insurance and a surety bond, and must later provide a list of subs and suppliers whose work exceeded $500.

facts.source: Idaho Code 45-507, 45-510
facts.fact: An Idaho claim of lien must be filed within 90 days after the claimant completes its labor or furnishes its last materials, and a copy served on the owner within 5 business days after filing. The lien expires 6 months after filing unless a suit to enforce it is commenced.

facts.source: Illinois local licensing (e.g., City of Chicago Department of Buildings)
facts.fact: Illinois has no statewide general contractor license; general contractors are licensed or registered by municipalities (Chicago, for example, licenses general contractors by class). Electrical and HVAC licensing is also local, while the state licenses roofers (IDFPR) and plumbers (IDPH).
facts.note: Widely reported and consistent with the state statutes reviewed, but no official state page stating 'no state GC license' was confirmed this session.

facts.source: 225 ILCS 335 (Illinois Roofing Industry Licensing Act); IDFPR
facts.fact: All Illinois roofing contractors must be licensed by the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR). A limited license covers residential properties of 8 units or less; an unlimited license covers residential, commercial and industrial work. The qualifying party must pass a state exam that includes Illinois roofing law.
facts.note: Statute text via Justia: https://law.justia.com/codes/illinois/chapter-225/act-225-ilcs-335/ (Act scheduled for repeal Jan. 1, 2031).

facts.fact: Illinois roofing contractors must post a continuous surety bond of $10,000 for a limited license or $25,000 for an unlimited license, and carry public liability and property damage insurance (amounts set by IDFPR) plus workers' compensation.

facts.source: Illinois Department of Public Health, Plumbing Program
facts.fact: Illinois plumbers are licensed statewide by the Illinois Department of Public Health. Apprentice plumbers must work under a licensed plumber for at least 4 years (48 to 72 months, 6 years maximum) before taking the state exam. Any licensed plumber who works for others must also register annually as a plumbing contractor and carry liability and workers' comp insurance.
facts.note: https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/environmental-health-protection/plumbing.html . Plumber licenses renew by April 30 each year with annual CE (hours not stated on the page).

facts.source: 815 ILCS 513 (Home Repair and Remodeling Act)
facts.fact: Illinois home repair contractors must carry liability insurance of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per occurrence for bodily injury and $50,000 per occurrence for property damage, plus $10,000 for work not meeting code; this is waived with a net worth of at least $1,000,000. Jobs over $1,000 need a written contract and a signed acknowledgment of the 'Home Repair: Know Your Consumer Rights' pamphlet.

An Illinois contractor must record its claim for lien (or sue) within 4 months after completion to keep the lien good against third parties such as lenders and buyers; against the owner, it may record within 2 years. A suit to enforce must be filed within 2 years after completion, and the contractor must give the owner a sworn statement listing all subs and suppliers before being paid.

Illinois subcontractors must serve the owner and lender a notice of claim within 90 days after completing their work. On an existing owner-occupied single-family home, subs must notify the occupant within 60 days of first furnishing. If the owner serves a written demand, the lien claimant must sue within 30 days or lose the lien.

facts.source: Indiana local licensing (city/county building departments)
facts.fact: Indiana has no statewide general contractor license; general contractors, electricians and HVAC contractors are licensed or registered by cities and counties (for example Indianapolis/Marion County). Plumbing is the main construction trade licensed statewide.
facts.note: Consistent with Indiana PLA's profession list and widely reported, but not confirmed on an official page stating there is no state GC license.

facts.source: Ind. Code 25-28.5-1-12; Indiana Plumbing Commission (Professional Licensing Agency)
facts.fact: Indiana plumbers are licensed statewide by the Indiana Plumbing Commission through the Professional Licensing Agency (PLA) as journeyman plumbers and plumbing contractors. Journeyman applicants need 4 years in a commission-approved apprenticeship or 4 years of qualifying plumbing experience; contractor applicants may also qualify with 4 years under a licensed plumbing contractor. Both must pass an exam.

facts.source: Indiana Professional Licensing Agency, Plumbing Commission page
facts.fact: Indiana plumbing exams are administered by PROV, which publishes the Indiana Plumbing Examinations Candidate Information Bulletin at provexam.com.

facts.source: Ind. Code 32-28-3-3
facts.fact: An Indiana lien claimant must record a sworn statement and notice of intention to hold a lien with the county recorder within 90 days after last performing labor or furnishing materials, or within 60 days for work on a Class 2 structure (generally 1- and 2-family dwellings and townhouses) and its accessory improvements.
facts.note: Statute text via Justia: https://law.justia.com/codes/indiana/title-32/article-28/chapter-3/section-32-28-3-3/ . Class 2 structure is defined in IC 22-12-1-5.

facts.fact: In Indiana, a supplier who furnishes labor or materials on credit to someone other than the owner must give the owner written notice within 30 days after first delivery for alteration or repair of an owner-occupied 1- or 2-family dwelling, or within 60 days (and file a copy with the county recorder) for original construction of such a dwelling, or it cannot acquire a lien.

facts.source: Ind. Code 32-28-3-6
facts.fact: A complaint to foreclose an Indiana mechanic's lien must be filed within 1 year after the notice of intention to hold a lien was recorded (or after a qualifying credit expires); otherwise the lien is void.

facts.source: Iowa Code 91C.1, 91C.2; Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing (Division of Labor) contractor registration
facts.fact: Iowa has no general contractor competency license or exam; instead, every person in the business of construction who earns $2,000 or more a year must register as a contractor with the state labor division and renew annually. Contractors with employees must file a workers' compensation certificate of insurance.

facts.source: Iowa Code 91C.2, 91C.7; Iowa contractor registration required documents
facts.fact: Out-of-state contractors registering in Iowa must file a $25,000 surety bond (or proof of Iowa DOT bid prequalification). The bond secures Iowa taxes and unemployment contributions and stays in force until the surety gives at least 30 days' written notice of cancellation.
keywords: iowa out of state contractor bond

facts.source: Iowa Admin. Code r. 661-502.2 (Electrical Examining Board)
facts.fact: Iowa licenses electricians statewide through the Electrical Examining Board: class A master and journeyman, residential master, residential electrician, special electrician and apprentice. A class A journeyman typically completes a registered 4-year apprenticeship and scores at least 70 on the exam; a class A master needs one year as a licensed journeyman plus a 70 on the master exam. An electrical contractor must hold or employ an active master.
facts.note: Rule text via Cornell LII: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/iowa/Iowa-Admin-Code-r-661-502-2 . Iowa renumbered these rules after the 2023 agency reorganization (now under DIAL, 481 IAC), so the version shown may not be current.

facts.source: Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board (DIAL)
facts.fact: The Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board licenses apprentices, journeypersons, masters and contractors in plumbing and mechanical disciplines (HVAC, refrigeration, hydronic, sheet metal). A master license requires a journeyperson license plus two years of journey-level experience (or a master license from another jurisdiction) and passing the board's master exam, given through Kirkwood Community College.

facts.source: Iowa Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board CE page
facts.fact: Iowa plumbing and mechanical licenses are issued for 3-year periods expiring June 30 (valid through August 31). Renewing a single journeyperson, master or specialty license requires 8 hours of continuing education.

facts.source: Iowa Code 572.13A, 572.13B
facts.fact: On Iowa residential construction, the general contractor must post a notice of commencement of work to the state Mechanics' Notice and Lien Registry (MNLR) within 10 days after work begins. A subcontractor must post a preliminary notice to the MNLR before the owner pays the balance to the general contractor, or it has no lien.

Iowa mechanic's liens are posted to the MNLR. A subcontractor who posts more than 90 days after its last labor or materials can recover only what the owner still owes the general contractor when notified. The absolute posting deadline is 2 years and 90 days after last furnishing, and an enforcement action must be brought within 2 years after that 90-day period ends.

facts.source: Kansas local licensing (city/county)
facts.fact: Kansas has no statewide general contractor license, and electrical, plumbing and HVAC licenses are also issued locally by cities and counties (for example Wichita/Sedgwick County or Johnson County), commonly using ICC exams. Roofing contractors are the notable statewide registration.
facts.note: Widely reported and consistent with the Kansas statutes reviewed, but not confirmed on an official state page stating there is no state GC or trade license.

facts.source: K.S.A. 50-6,121 to 50-6,138 (Kansas Roofing Registration Act)
facts.fact: Under the Kansas Roofing Registration Act, anyone in the business of roofing in Kansas must hold a roofing contractor registration certificate, administered by the Attorney General, and an unregistered roofer may not bring or maintain a court claim related to its roofing business. The AG sets insurance or bond requirements by rule.

A Kansas contractor who contracts with the owner must file a verified lien statement with the clerk of the district court within 4 months after last furnishing labor or materials. On non-residential property, filing a notice of extension within those 4 months extends the deadline to 5 months; the extension is not available on residential property (1- or 2-family residence).

A Kansas subcontractor or supplier must file its lien statement within 3 months after last furnishing labor or materials, naming the contractor, and serve a copy on an owner. On non-residential property, a notice of extension filed within 3 months extends the deadline to 5 months.

On new Kansas residential property, a lien claimant who wants to keep lien rights against a good-faith buyer must file a notice of intent to perform with the district court clerk before the deed is recorded. The notice lapses 18 months after filing unless a lien is filed within that time.
keywords: kansas notice of intent to perform

facts.fact: An action to foreclose a Kansas mechanic's lien must be brought within one year after the lien statement is filed (or within one year of a promissory note's maturity if a note was attached instead).

facts.source: Kentucky local licensing; Kentucky Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (HBC)
facts.fact: Kentucky has no statewide general contractor license; general and residential contractors are licensed or registered locally (for example by Louisville Metro or Lexington-Fayette). The state Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (HBC) licenses electricians, plumbers, HVAC, boiler and fire sprinkler/alarm contractors.
facts.note: HBC's trade list is on https://dhbc.ky.gov/ , but no official page stating there is no state GC license was found this session.

facts.source: KRS 227A.060 (amended eff. July 15, 2024); 815 KAR 35:060
facts.fact: Kentucky licenses electrical contractors, master electricians and electricians statewide. An electrician needs 8,000 hours of verifiable electrical experience and a master electrician needs 16,000 hours (counted from age 16, with limited substitutions for schooling or teaching), and each must pass an exam (70% minimum per regulation). An electrical contractor must carry at least $1,000,000 in general liability insurance plus workers' comp.
facts.note: Statute text via Justia (2025 code): https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-227a/section-227a-060/ ; 70% score from 815 KAR 35:060 (the version read was marked superseded): https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/815/035/060/14586/

facts.fact: Kentucky electrical licenses are valid for one year and renew by the last day of the licensee's birth month, with annual continuing education required under 815 KAR 2:010.
facts.note: From 815 KAR 35:060 (Dec. 5, 2023 version), which the legislature site marks as superseded: https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/815/035/060/14586/ . Confirm against the current version; CE hours were not stated.

facts.fact: Kentucky issues master and journeyman plumber licenses statewide; no master or journeyman license is issued without passing a department exam with written and practical (hands-on) parts, and applicants must be at least 18.
facts.note: Statute text via Justia (2025 code): https://law.justia.com/codes/kentucky/chapter-318/section-318-040/ . Administered by HBC per https://dhbc.ky.gov/

facts.fact: Kentucky licenses master HVAC contractors and journeyman HVAC mechanics. A journeyman needs at least 2 years of HVAC work under a master HVAC contractor; a master needs 2 years as a master contractor or equivalent, 2 years as a journeyman under a master, or 2 years as a licensed mechanical engineer. Both must pass a department exam.

In Kentucky, a lien claimant without a direct contract with the owner must give the owner written notice of intent to claim a lien within 75 days after last furnishing for claims under $1,000, or within 120 days for claims over $1,000. On an owner-occupied single- or two-family dwelling, the notice is due within 75 days.

A Kentucky lien statement must be filed with the county clerk within 6 months after the claimant stops furnishing labor or materials, and a copy mailed to the owner within 7 days of filing or the lien dissolves. The lien is dissolved unless an enforcement action is filed within 12 months after the statement is filed.

facts.source: AS 08.18.011; Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing (Construction Contractors)
facts.fact: Alaska has no project-value threshold for general registration: under AS 08.18.011 a person may not bid on or work as a contractor until registered with the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. A general contractor also may not contract with an unregistered specialty contractor.
facts.note: Contractor statutes PDF from the division: https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/Portals/5/pub/ContractorStatutes.pdf ; program page https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/cbpl/ProfessionalLicensing/ConstructionContractors.aspx

facts.source: Alaska CBPL Construction Contractors program page; 12 AAC 21
facts.fact: Alaska registration types include General, Residential, Specialty (limited to no more than three trades), Mechanical, Electrical and Handyman. A Handyman registration is limited to projects where the total contract price, including labor and materials, is $10,000 or less per project.

facts.source: AS 08.18.025; Alaska CBPL Residential Endorsement Exam page
facts.fact: An Alaska general contractor needs a Residential Contractor Endorsement to build or alter (changes worth more than 25% of the structure's value) privately owned residential buildings of 1 to 4 units. The endorsement requires passing the residential endorsement exam (scheduled through PSI, results good for 1 year) and completing the 16-hour cold climate course (Alaska Craftsman Home Program or equivalent) within the prior two years.

facts.source: AS 08.18.071; Alaska CBPL Bond and Insurance Quick Facts
facts.fact: Alaska contractor registration bonds are $25,000 for a general contractor, $20,000 for a general contractor with a residential endorsement, $10,000 for mechanical and specialty contractors, and $5,000 for a handyman (contracts of $10,000 or less).

Alaska contractors must carry public liability and property damage insurance of at least $20,000 property damage, $50,000 for injury or death of one person, and $100,000 for injury or death of more than one person, plus workers' compensation as required by AS 23.30. A handyman's projects of $2,500 or less do not require the liability insurance.
facts.note: Statute text in the division's PDF https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/Portals/5/pub/ContractorStatutes.pdf ; amounts also on https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/Portals/5/pub/CON_BondInsuranceQuickFacts.pdf

facts.fact: In Alaska, a contractor who was not registered when the contract was made cannot sue to collect compensation or enforce a contract for work that requires registration.

facts.source: Alaska Dept. of Labor and Workforce Development, Mechanical Inspection licensing requirements; Alaska CBPL Electrical Administrators
facts.fact: Alaska electrical work requires two layers: the Department of Labor issues Certificates of Fitness (journeyman electrician, residential wireman, power lineman, trainee), and an electrical contractor must have an Electrical Administrator (a supervisory license from CBPL) assigned. A journeyman electrician certificate requires 8,000 hours of commercial/industrial electrical experience as a trainee and a 70% exam score.

facts.source: Alaska Dept. of Labor and Workforce Development, Mechanical Inspection licensing requirements; Alaska CBPL Construction Contractors
facts.fact: Alaska plumbers need a Department of Labor Certificate of Fitness (journeyman plumber, gas plumber, restricted utility, trainee); journeyman plumber requires 8,000 hours of plumbing installation as a trainee and a 70% exam. A mechanical contractor (plumbing, heating, sheet metal, refrigeration) must have a Mechanical Administrator license assigned.

facts.source: Alaska Dept. of Labor Mechanical Inspection; 12 AAC 21.650; CBPL License Expiration Dates
facts.fact: Alaska journeyman electrician and journeyman plumber certificates last 2 years and need 16 CE hours per 24 months (at least 8 on code changes). Residential Contractor Endorsement renewal needs 16 contact hours of continuing competency. Construction contractor registrations currently expire September 30, 2028.

In Alaska, a notice of right to lien given to the owner before furnishing work shifts the burden to the owner to prove it did not know of or agree to the work. A claim of lien must be recorded within 120 days after the claimant completes or stops work; if the owner records a notice of completion, claimants who did not give a notice of right to lien must record within 15 days after it.
facts.note: Statute text via FindLaw: https://codes.findlaw.com/ak/title-34-property/ak-st-sect-34-35-068 and https://codes.findlaw.com/ak/title-34-property/ak-st-sect-34-35-064 . The 120-day period (formerly 90) is confirmed by the official 2010 session law (HB 253, SLA 2010 ch. 51): https://www.akleg.gov/pdf/billfiles/SLAs/sl10pdfs/CH051.pdf

facts.fact: An Alaska claim of lien stops binding the property 6 months after it is recorded unless a suit to enforce it is filed within that 6 months, or an extension notice is recorded during that period, which extends it another 6 months.

facts.source: Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors (LSLBC), Types of Licenses; La. R.S. 37:2150.1
facts.fact: Louisiana licenses contractors statewide through the Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors (LSLBC). A commercial license is required for commercial projects valued at $50,000 or more (labor and materials), and that threshold also applies to subcontractors and specialty trades on commercial jobs.

facts.source: LSLBC Types of Licenses; SB 392 (2024 Reg. Session) digest amending La. R.S. 37:2150.1
facts.fact: Effective August 1, 2024, Louisiana lowered the residential building contractor license trigger from $75,000 to $50,000 for new residential structures and for home improvement work on existing homes over that amount. Home improvement work from $7,500 up to $50,000 requires a home improvement registration instead.
facts.note: https://lslbc.louisiana.gov/types-of-licenses ; https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1364300 (board page says 'over $50,000', the bill digest says '$50,000 or greater' for new residential)

facts.source: LSLBC Types of Licenses
facts.fact: In Louisiana, electrical, mechanical (HVAC), and plumbing projects over $10,000 require an LSLBC license, and asbestos, hazardous waste, lead abatement, and underground storage tank work requires a license at any value ($1 or more). Residential swimming pool work over $7,500 and mold remediation of $7,500 or more also need their own classifications.

facts.source: HB 953 (Act 908, 2026 Regular Session) digest; State Plumbing Board of Louisiana website
facts.fact: Act 908 of 2026 abolishes the State Plumbing Board of Louisiana and moves plumbing licensing to a Plumbing Contractors Subcommittee of the Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors, fully effective January 1, 2027. Plumber licenses issued by the old board through December 31, 2026 become equivalent LSLBC licenses on that date. Individuals are licensed as apprentice, journeyman, or master plumbers, and businesses as plumbing contractors (including master and residential plumbing contractors).
facts.note: https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1486872 (Act 908 digest) ; https://spbla.com/ notes the transfer. Insurance and other plumbing rules may change under the new subcommittee's rules, so recheck after January 1, 2027.

facts.source: LSLBC FAQ; LSLBC Checklist of Items Required for Initial License; LSLBC General Candidate Information Bulletin
facts.fact: Every Louisiana license applicant's qualifying party must complete the LSLBC's online Business and Law course, which is taken from the candidate's own computer rather than scheduled at a test center. Trade exams for classifications that need them are scheduled through PSI after the board sends an eligibility letter.
facts.note: https://www.lslbc.gov/faq/ ; https://lslbc.gov/checklist-of-items-required-for-initial-license-and-to-maintain-license/ ; https://lslbc.louisiana.gov/wp-content/uploads/cib_General.pdf. Older prep material describes a proctored open-book Business and Law exam; the board now calls it a course.

facts.source: LSLBC Checklist of Items Required for Initial License; LSLBC FAQ
facts.fact: Louisiana residential and home improvement license holders must carry at least $100,000 in general liability insurance plus workers' compensation coverage, and the insurer emails certificates to the board at application and renewal. The checklist states commercial applicants do not have to submit insurance certificates.

facts.source: LSLBC Financial Statement form
facts.fact: Every Louisiana license applicant files an LSLBC Financial Statement prepared by a CPA, bookkeeper or accountant and dated within 12 months of the application. The board form lists minimum net worth of $50,000 for residential and commercial applicants (other than commercial labor-only) and $25,000 for home improvement, mold remediation and commercial labor-only applicants.
facts.note: Net worth figures came from https://lslbc.gov/wp-content/uploads/Financial-Statement.pdf; a newer 2025 version of the form would not load, and older sources cite a lower $10,000 commercial figure. Confirm the current minimum with LSLBC.

facts.source: La. R.S. 9:4822 (Private Works Act)
facts.fact: Under the Louisiana Private Works Act, if no notice of contract was filed, a claimant must file its statement of claim or privilege within 60 days after a notice of termination is filed, or after substantial completion or abandonment if none is filed. If a notice of contract was timely filed, subcontractor and supplier claimants get 30 days after the notice of termination (or 6 months after substantial completion if none), and the general contractor gets 60 days (or 7 months).

For residential work in Louisiana with no timely notice of contract, the filing deadline stretches to 70 days, but only if the claimant gives the owner a written notice of nonpayment before the normal 60-day period ends and at least 10 days before filing the statement of claim.
A Louisiana Private Works Act claim or privilege is extinguished if the claimant does not file suit against the owner to enforce it within one year after filing the statement of claim or privilege.

facts.source: LSLBC FAQ
facts.fact: A new Louisiana contractor license is valid for one year, after which it may be renewed for a one-, two-, or three-year period. Residential construction license holders must complete at least 6 hours of continuing education each year from a board-approved provider, though holding certain major commercial classifications satisfies the requirement.

facts.source: Maine Office of the Attorney General, Home Construction Contracts consumer page
facts.fact: Maine has no statewide license for general or home building contractors; the Attorney General's office states that Maine does not license or regulate home contractors. Any local registration requirements come from individual municipalities.

facts.source: Home Construction Contracts Act, 10 M.R.S. §1486 et seq.; Maine Attorney General
facts.fact: Maine's Home Construction Contracts Act requires a written contract for any home construction or improvement job over $3,000. The contract must include a warranty statement, and the down payment is capped at one-third of the total contract price.

facts.source: Maine Electricians' Examining Board, Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation
facts.fact: The Maine Electricians' Examining Board licenses electricians statewide at master, journeyman, journeyman-in-training, apprentice, and helper levels, plus limited licenses. Approved candidates take the board's exams through the vendor PROV, Inc.

facts.source: Maine Electricians' Examining Board, Master Electrician licensing page
facts.fact: A Maine master electrician needs a 576-hour education program (nine 45-hour courses including a current NEC course, plus 126 hours of related coursework) and either 4,000 hours as a licensed journeyman or 12,000 hours of electrical installation experience, and must pass the exam. Maine has electrician reciprocity agreements with New Hampshire and Vermont.

facts.source: Maine Electricians' Examining Board, Master Electrician licensing page
facts.fact: Maine electrician licenses run two years from the date of first licensure and renew biennially. Renewal requires completion of the board-adopted 15-hour current National Electrical Code update course.

facts.source: Maine Plumbers' Examining Board, Individual Licenses page
facts.fact: The Maine Plumbers' Examining Board licenses master, journeyman, journeyman-in-training, and trainee plumbers, with licenses renewing every two years. A journeyman needs 4,000 hours over at least two years as a licensed trainee under a master, and a master needs 2,000 hours as a licensed journeyman over at least one year (or 8,000 hours over four years as a trainee).

facts.source: Maine Fuel Board, Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation
facts.fact: Maine has no general HVAC license; heating fuel work is regulated by the Maine Fuel Board. It licenses master, journeyman, and apprentice oil burner and/or solid fuel technicians, propane and natural gas technicians, and limited licenses such as tank installers and wood pellet technicians.

In Maine, a mechanics' lien claimant who wants to preserve the lien by recording must file a lien statement in the registry of deeds within 90 days after it stops performing labor, furnishing materials, or providing services.

A Maine mechanics' lien must be enforced by filing a court action within 120 days after the last labor or services were performed or materials furnished. If the claimant has no contract with the owner, the owner's total liability is capped at the balance still owed to the owner's contractor when the owner receives notice or is served, whichever comes first.

facts.source: Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC), Maryland Department of Labor; Md. Code, Business Regulation Title 8
facts.fact: Maryland's main statewide contractor license is the Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) license, which is required for anyone who performs or agrees to perform home improvement work for a homeowner. MHIC issues contractor, subcontractor, and salesperson licenses.

facts.source: Secondary licensing guides (no official confirmation found)
facts.fact: Maryland does not issue a statewide license for commercial general contractors or new home builders; commercial GC requirements are set by individual counties and cities. New home builders register separately with the Office of the Attorney General.
